screens.name: Home — settled, enlarged and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 32–33 show the seated orb, question plaque, omen and navigation, while supplied runtime evidence reports hero geometry, contrast and navigation-clearance checks.
findings: Consolidate the question plaque and “Touch the Ball” into a clearer visual invitation so the orb, instruction and omen compete less at 200%.

screens.name: Home — omen success fixture, unavailable and policy expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 32–33 show distinct available, unavailable and expanded-policy treatments with explicit attempt and reading-credit language.
findings: Separate the omen status, recovery timing and policy into tighter centered groups to reduce the expanded card’s visual dominance.

screens.name: Home — room destination controls
screens.evidence: Sheet 49 shows Shelf, Hearth and Cabinet as framed thumbnails beneath the omen, and runtime evidence reports all three routes and minimum 44×44 targets passing.
findings: Give the thumbnail frames contact shadows and shared room lighting so they feel mounted in the apothecary rather than inserted as an image menu.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheets 36–37 show the centered age question, explicit birthday-free confirmation and separate under-13 action at both text scales.
findings: Increase the primary plank’s edge and contact-shadow definition against the shelf while preserving the concise two-choice layout.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 show labeled day, month and year fields, optional Skip and a two-row enlarged layout.
findings: Group the optional label and Skip more closely with the birthday fields so their relationship remains immediate at both scales.

screens.name: Age restriction — onboarding and birthday-edit blocked states
screens.evidence: Sheets 1 and 38 show a clear age restriction with a correction action, supported by reported browser restriction and correction checks.
findings: Shorten the supporting explanation within its centered grouping to reduce the large-text screen’s repetitive vertical stack.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheet 39 shows the correction requirement, labeled date inputs, Check birthday and a return action that extends below the enlarged capture.
findings: Reduce the spacing between the requirement and date group so the return action requires less scrolling at 200%.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected, optional and selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 39–41 show four parchment choices, optional Skip, a selected checkmark and the changed Save focus and continue action.
findings: Tighten enlarged option padding and shorten the confirmation label so the primary action and Back are easier to discover together.

screens.name: Birthday editing — populated valid state
screens.evidence: Sheet 64 shows populated fields, Save, Cancel and collapsed removal, while runtime evidence reports save/reload, cancellation and focus checks at both scales.
findings: Use a clearer centered separation between reversible editing actions and birthday removal.

screens.name: Birthday editing — invalid calendar date and partial input
screens.evidence: Sheets 1–2 show field edges and specific date or missing-day errors, with reported invalid-field semantics and browser checks.
findings: Reduce helper-copy height above the fields so enlarged validation does not push Cancel and removal so far below Save.

screens.name: Birth details — initial and empty birth time
screens.evidence: Sheets 8–9 and 63 show an optional local-time field, a 24-hour example, Continue to city and an unknown-time alternative.
findings: Combine the time-format guidance into a shorter centered example to reduce repeated explanation at 200%.

screens.name: Birth details — invalid time
screens.evidence: Sheet 9 shows 25:99 with a distinct field outline and the accepted 00:00–23:59 range, supported by reported validation and focus checks.
findings: Maintain this specific recovery message while making the error outline more visually distinct from the gold focus outline.

screens.name: Birth details — forgotten confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheet 8 explicitly confirms that time and place were forgotten while the birthday was kept, and runtime evidence reports the forget flow passing.
findings: Give the confirmation its own compact centered status group so it does not merge with the form instructions.

screens.name: Birth details — empty city and retained city draft
screens.evidence: Sheets 6–7 and 62–63 show empty and Copenhagen-populated city fields, optional Skip and data-sharing guidance, with reported Back-preserved drafts.
findings: Move the selection instruction closer to the field and shorten its wording to reduce the gap between entry and the next step.

screens.name: Birth details — city service failure and no results
screens.evidence: Sheets 7–8 distinguish service failure from no matching city, and runtime evidence reports injected 503/no-result cases and successful recovery.
findings: Condense the saved-chart reassurance and no-result guidance into separate short centered groups to keep recovery controls nearer the field.

screens.name: Birth details — live city results
screens.evidence: Sheets 9–10 show multiple Copenhagen results separated into city and region/country groups, with reported live lookup and full accessible labels.
findings: Make city and region more distinct through weight and spacing so enlarged result cards remain quickly comparable.

screens.name: Birth profile — calculated, saved and recovered result
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show saved Moon/rising results, location/time, Done, Edit and Forget, supported by reported calculation and reload checks.
findings: Present Moon and rising as two short centered groups to avoid the oversized three-line combined result.

screens.name: Ask approach — input-method choice
screens.evidence: Sheet 3 shows the orb seated on the table above Type a question and Speak a question, including an enlarged heading that wraps over the table edge.
findings: Reserve a consistent heading region below the orb so enlarged “Your question” stays visually separate from the table and writing action.

screens.name: Ask — populated self question and collapsed context
screens.evidence: Sheets 4 and 6 show the subject, collapsed disclosure, populated paper input, expanded-editor action and primary submission, with reported contrast and draft checks.
findings: Reduce the vertical gap between the subject and disclosure so the question remains the dominant starting point.

screens.name: Ask — expanded personal context
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4 and 34 show expanded sharing details taking most of the enlarged viewport before the question field.
findings: Compress the disclosure into short centered data groups with one concise sharing statement so users can reach their question with less scanning.

screens.name: Ask — named-person selection and populated name
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6 show Myself/Someone selection, Alex, a privacy explanation and explicit confirmation, with reported subject-validation and focus checks.
findings: Shorten the centered privacy explanation so the enlarged confirmation action sits closer to the name field.

screens.name: Ask — constrained named-person empty and valid fixtures
screens.evidence: Sheet 35 shows constrained person forms with the confirmation area outside the crop, and the nominal empty fixture displays Alex without a visible validation message.
findings: Add a captured empty-name validation result with the recovery action visible to make this specific state independently assessable.

screens.name: Ask — named-person question with collapsed details
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–5 show About Alex and the matching populated question across normal, enlarged and transition captures.
findings: Give the subject-change affordance slightly stronger separation from its label while retaining the centered arrangement.

screens.name: Ask — constrained typing and long question
screens.evidence: Sheets 34–35 show reachable submission and expanded-editor controls beside internally cropped long text, with reported full-draft retention and scroll cues.
findings: Keep a small inset at the scroll viewport’s top and bottom so cropped letterforms do not touch the paper edge.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — questions 1, 2 and 3 unselected
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–13 show numbered progress, three radio choices, custom-answer access and disabled Continue or Reveal, supported by reported keyboard navigation.
findings: Align the radio indicator’s visual spacing consistently with the centered labels, especially when labels grow at 200%.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — selected answer
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows the Time radio filled and Continue visibly enabled at both scales, with reported keyboard selection and focus checks.
findings: Add a restrained selected edge treatment to make the chosen parchment easier to identify across the full row.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — empty custom answer
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 show the custom-answer paper, Expand editor, explicit minimum-entry guidance and disabled Continue.
findings: Keep the minimum-entry guidance close to the input so the reason for the disabled action is understood before reaching the button.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — populated custom answer and constrained long answer
screens.evidence: Sheet 34 shows a populated final answer with Reveal and a long answer scrolled inside the constrained paper field.
findings: Add stronger internal scroll-edge spacing so the enlarged answer reads as intentionally scrollable rather than cut by the paper frame.

screens.name: Expanded editor — populated custom answer across all pictured sizes
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–22 show 300-character drafts with Cancel and Done across 360/390/430 widths and 500/844 heights, supported by all 24 reported editor combinations passing.
findings: Inset the centered text from scrolling edges and increase line separation slightly to reduce the dense repeated-text appearance at 200%.

screens.name: Expanded editor — populated long question across all pictured sizes
screens.evidence: Sheets 22–25 show 489/500-character questions with visible counters and footer actions, and runtime evidence reports draft preservation, focus return and at least 208px enlarged writing space.
findings: Preserve a visible text inset at scroll boundaries so partial first and last lines do not appear clipped against the decorative sheet.

screens.name: Voice — unavailable and retry
screens.evidence: Sheet 36 shows an explicit unavailable state with microphone guidance, a primary typing fallback and a separate retry action.
findings: Make the microphone-permission guidance more directly actionable within the browser if retry encounters the same restriction.

screens.name: Loading — planning and research
screens.evidence: Sheets 45–46 distinguish Finding the thread from Reading the signs and show timing, credit protection and Cancel, with reported reduced-motion and timing checks.
findings: Strengthen the visual distinction between the two loading stages without adding more explanatory text.

screens.name: Reading errors — planning and prediction recovery
screens.evidence: Sheets 25–27 show Try again, editing and prediction-stage answer review with no-charge reassurance, supported by reported live recoverable-error checks.
findings: Give the error heading and recovery group slightly tighter spacing so the recovery path reads as one unit.

screens.name: Sensitive question — planning and prediction redirects
screens.evidence: Sheets 50–51 show the support destination, alternate question actions and no-credit/no-memory reassurance, with reported live sensitive-path checks.
findings: Place a short centered reason nearer the heading so users understand the redirect before encountering the support button.

screens.name: Opening — normal and golden timed states
screens.evidence: Sheets 41–42 show painted orb opening frames and settled forecasts, while runtime evidence reports seven modes, save-once behavior, interruption and reduced-motion checks.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — settled and expanded actions
screens.evidence: Sheets 46–49 show the forecast, uncertainty label, check-in date and several equal-weight action links, with enlarged secondary actions extending below the viewport.

screens.name: Why this forecast — full explanation

screens.name: Reading details — explanation expanded

screens.name: Reading details — answers expanded

screens.name: Reading details — assumptions expanded
screens.evidence: Sheet 28 shows the selected assumptions disclosure, condition label, body and explicit close action.

screens.name: Check-in — unanswered

screens.name: Check-in — selected but unsaved

components.name: Age confirmation control

components.name: Modal shell and fixed footer
components.evidence: Sheets 19–25 and 52–57 show constrained modal content with persistent editor or Done actions, including partially visible footer-adjacent text in some enlarged captures.
findings: Increase content clearance above fixed footers and preserve a visible inset at scrolling boundaries.

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments based on the supplied screenshots and runtime narrative; no tools, source, prior ratings or other task state were inspected.

For each item, A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is round(0.4A + 0.6F, 1), excluding genuinely inapplicable null dimensions.

The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across all screens and components; the most persistent browser deficiencies are enlarged-content hierarchy, dense centered explanations and inconsistent physical integration of interface surfaces.
Reported runtime checks support functionality beyond the still images, but their underlying action logs, recordings and measured contrast samples were not independently inspected.

Transition screenshots support comparison of composition, not direct observation of animation, parallax, camera speed, lighting changes or temporal occlusion; the supplied performance and reduced-motion results remain reported evidence.
Below-viewport content and deliberately scrolled screenshots are not automatically inaccessible; no hard-gate failure is established by these captures given the reported reachability checks.
The named-person empty fixture does not visibly demonstrate an empty-name validation result, despite reported subject-validation coverage.
No specific press-state captures or complete browser assistive-technology drive are supplied; zero axe violations alone do not establish complete accessibility.

Physical iPhone/VoiceOver, native keyboard, haptics, tilt, real OS sharing and native performance remain deferred without deductions solely for that boundary; these scores do not certify native 9/10 quality.
Connected Circles behavior and real billing are unverified, system sharing uses a boundary mock, and browser reminders explicitly remain unscheduled.
Synthetic prediction, source, error and date fixtures were treated as layout evidence rather than production-copy defects or proof of predictive quality.
The retained failed editor-height and share-coordinate observations are acknowledged as reported failures followed by reported corrections, rather than erased from the evidence.
topFixes: Shorten enlarged headings and supporting copy, then tighten grouping so primary actions remain close to their inputs without reducing the requested text scale.
Break long explanations into short centered sections with descriptive subheadings and consistent paragraph spacing.
Add internal scroll-edge padding and more clearance above fixed footers, particularly for enlarged editors and invitation View link controls.
Give wood actions, room thumbnails and floating illustrations consistent edge thickness, contact shadows and room lighting.
Reduce decorative height in history rows, profile cards, plan options and disclosure headers to improve comparison and navigation at 200%.
Strengthen the next-action hierarchy on reveal and sharing screens instead of presenting many equally weighted gold links.
Capture the missing empty-name recovery state and directly review camera/opening recordings before awarding premium continuity scores.
